manual.title: AGY Manual
manual.topic.1.label: Start Here
manual.topic.1.note: what agy pro adds, and the first three steps
manual.topic.1.p1: agy pro is a helper in front of the real agy CLI. It keeps providers, models, run presets and prompts in one place, and it can run several models side by side.
manual.topic.1.p2: Start with `agy pro setup` in a terminal. On a real console this opens the full-screen setup; a pipe or a redirect gets the line wizard instead, because nothing can answer a full screen there.
manual.topic.1.p3: Then add one provider (hub row [1]), set a default preset if you run fanout, and keep using agy the way you always did. Every other command passes through to the real agy.
manual.topic.1.p4: Nothing is written without consent. A write shows its exact diff and waits for y/N, and `--yes` is the stand-in when a script cannot answer.
manual.topic.2.label: Providers
manual.topic.2.note: one endpoint per row, and the key stays in the environment
manual.topic.2.p1: A provider is one API endpoint the swarm can call. The registry stores its name, its base URL, and the NAME of the environment variable that holds the key. Key material is refused in every field.
manual.topic.2.p2: Open hub row [1]. Enter on a provider shows its models. The Add provider row opens a form with three fields, a read-only defaults block and a Save row; Enter on Save shows the diff.
manual.topic.2.p3: The Test, Edit and Delete rows act on the provider the cursor last rested on. Delete is a danger row: it re-reads providers.json and refuses if that entry changed while the gate was open.
manual.topic.2.p4: The form refuses a duplicate name, a bare http URL (loopback excepted), and a value that looks like a key. Nothing is written until you answer y.
manual.topic.3.label: Presets
manual.topic.3.note: saved fanout run settings, not a prompt or a seat list
manual.topic.3.p1: A preset is a named run config: seat count, tool set, turn limit and time budget. It is not a prompt, and it is not a list of seats.
manual.topic.3.p2: Open hub row [2]. Enter opens the editor: two field grids around an allow_hosts list, with a read-only source column naming the rung that supplies each value.
manual.topic.3.p3: The New preset, Duplicate, Edit, Delete and Set default rows write fanout-presets.json. Set default needs the approval gate, and a corrupt file warns and asks before the first save replaces it.
manual.topic.4.label: Prompts
manual.topic.4.note: seven slots, an override file each, a source badge
manual.topic.4.p1: The prompt library holds seven slots: review, security, plan-audit, research, ideas, custom, and the native seat preamble. Each row carries the badge of the source in force.
manual.topic.4.p2: An override is one plain-text file per slot under the prompts directory (the storage section of Help lists the path). Compiled default, file and env are the three rungs, and env wins.
manual.topic.4.p3: Enter opens the editor for that slot. Save shows the content diff before it writes, and the reset row deletes the override so the compiled default returns.
manual.topic.5.label: Settings
manual.topic.5.note: eight sections, the [ro] badge, and the y/N gate
manual.topic.5.p1: Open hub row [4]. The grid holds eight sections: Launch & Profile, Models & Providers, Bridge Tools & Budgets, Swarm & Fanout, Diagnostics & Keys, Install & Update, Environment Variables, Appearance.
manual.topic.5.p2: A row marked [ro] is display only, and pressing it just explains itself. A danger row asks y/N, a choice row opens a numbered list, and a free-text row opens an inline editor.
manual.topic.5.p3: The block under the list shows the cursor row's value, default, source, note, choices and danger flag, so the state is readable before you press.
manual.topic.5.p4: In the editor Ctrl+S submits, Tab moves to OK, and Esc cancels. Language and the launcher menu are set in the Appearance section.
manual.topic.6.label: Doctor
manual.topic.6.note: a read-only report, and r retakes it
manual.topic.6.p1: Open hub row [5]. Tab switches between the Status pane and the Doctor pane. Status lists the mode, the profile, the real agy path, the registry summary, and env var names rather than their values.
manual.topic.6.p2: The Doctor pane renders the diagnose output: the real agy binary, the shim PATH location, state and directories, and provider key probes with the values masked.
manual.topic.6.p3: Both panes are read-only. Press r to run both reads again; no key here writes a file or starts a fix. Repairs live one screen away, in Settings under Diagnostics and Keys.
manual.topic.6.p4: The terminal twins are `agy pro settings doctor fix-keys all` and `agy pro settings doctor rollback-keys <backup-dir>`.
manual.topic.7.label: Language
manual.topic.7.note: twelve languages, applied at once, no restart
manual.topic.7.p1: Open hub row [7]. Every row shows the language's own name, so the list stays readable before any translation loads.
manual.topic.7.p2: Choosing writes the code to state.json and re-renders the whole app at once. There is no restart: the hub, the footer, and every screen opened afterwards follow.
manual.topic.7.p3: Arabic also flips the frame to a right-to-left layout. Text is drawn in logical order with right-aligned columns; visual reordering and Arabic shaping are not promised.
manual.topic.8.label: Dashboard
manual.topic.8.note: the Node dashboard's files, read and never probed
manual.topic.8.p1: Open hub row [8]. The screen reads the two files the Node dashboard writes and renders them: the server record and the usage snapshot.
manual.topic.8.p2: Rows: Start server, Refresh, Open in browser, Back. The Refresh row runs one bounded headless refresh and reloads the files; the Start server row asks for one guarded detached server, then re-reads the port.
manual.topic.8.p3: Every figure comes from the snapshot. A missing or stale snapshot says so instead of showing zeros, and the Open in browser row refuses while no port is known.
manual.topic.9.label: Integrations
manual.topic.9.note: five features, one diff, one y/N, then every write
manual.topic.9.p1: Open hub row [9]. Integrations manages five things agy pro can install for the real agy: the statusLine, hooks, rules, plugins and skills.
manual.topic.9.p2: Rows 1 to 5 toggle one feature each and carry two states side by side: the intent you recorded, and the posture the engine reads from disk. Unset is not off; unset means nothing was ever claimed.
manual.topic.9.p3: The action rows are writes. The Apply pending row deploys every feature whose intent is on, the Retract all row moves the files to a timestamped backup and records intent off, the Adopt row records only what is on disk.
manual.topic.9.p4: The Rollback row restores settings.json or one feature's pre-install tree from a snapshot, and the Repair row re-deploys the drifted and missing destinations while foreign files are named and left alone.
manual.topic.9.p5: The Preset row opens a native or tools choice, and a row marked >> opens a choice instead of composing a write. Every action shows one diff, takes one y/N, then runs the engine calls and the intent rows together.
manual.topic.10.label: CLI Basics
manual.topic.10.note: the verbs, the diff, --yes, and the exit codes
manual.topic.10.p1: Every verb lives under `agy pro`: setup, mode, status, models, swarm, settings, integrations, doctor, fanout, config, hybrid, version, help. A bare `agy pro` prints the verb table.
manual.topic.10.p2: A writing verb composes one plan, prints its exact diff, and asks y/N. On a pipe or a redirect nothing can answer, so it refuses and names `--yes`; add `--yes` after reading the diff.
manual.topic.10.p3: Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for a runtime error, and 2 for a usage or flag error. A refused or cancelled write changes nothing and says so.
manual.topic.10.p4: Anything agy pro does not own passes straight through to the real agy, so `agy -m ...` and `agy agents` keep working.
help.guide.line.1: agy pro puts providers, models, fanout presets and prompts in one place, in front of the real agy CLI.
help.guide.line.2: It can also install rules, skills, plugins, hooks and the statusLine for the real agy, and run several models side by side.
help.guide.line.3: Every write shows its exact diff and waits for y/N. The sections below name the keys, the storage files and the color tiers.
help.guide.manual: Press Enter to open the manual: ten pages, one per surface.

view.swarm.exclude_models.label: Model Exclusion List
view.swarm.exclude_models.note: one rule for every exclusion: auto-seating and failover skip an excluded entry, an explicit --models/--seats pick is honored with the warning that it is excluded, and nothing is ever rejected. Stored in providers.json defaults.excludeModels; when the key is absent or null the built-in default applies, shown here as the single entry family:k3, so saving that seeded list unchanged keeps the same rule, while an explicit empty list means you own an empty list and nothing is excluded. Read-only outside the hub; edit in the hub: agy pro setup.
settings.exclude.builtin_absent: the excludeModels key is absent or null, so the built-in default applies: the k3 family rule (family k3 or a k3 id token). An explicit empty list excludes nothing. The list below is that same rule written as the single entry family:k3, so saving it unchanged keeps the rule; add or remove entries to change it.
settings.exclude.owned: this list is user-owned: it replaces the built-in k3 default entirely.
settings.exclude.entries_empty: (no entries: nothing is excluded while the list stays user-owned)
settings.exclude.hint: Enter on an entry arms it. Enter on Add, Remove, or Save acts on the list. Esc returns.
settings.exclude.stale_base: providers.json defaults.excludeModels changed on disk since this editor opened. Nothing was written; the list was reloaded, so review it and save again.
settings.exclude.disk_check_failed: providers.json could not be re-read, so the on-disk check did not run. Nothing was written; retry.
settings.prompt.exclude_entry: Exclusion entry (provider name, model id, provider/model, or family:<name>)
settings.msg.exclude_none_armed: no entry selected: press Enter on an entry row first, then Remove entry.
settings.msg.exclude_unchanged: providers.json defaults.excludeModels already holds this list, so nothing was written.
settings.approval.exclude_models: Write the model exclusion list to providers.json defaults.excludeModels; auto-seating and failover read it on the next run.
settings.approval.exclude_absent: (the excludeModels key is absent or null today, so the built-in default applies and this write replaces it with the list below: the draft is the rule that applies from then on, and the entry family:k3 reproduces the built-in k3 rule)
